newsitem.title: USA: NYC to modify 97 budget, adds $450m in tax revenue.
newsitem.headline: NYC to modify 97 budget, adds $450m in tax revenue.

text.p: New York City officials are to announce a budget modification Thursday that they said included $450 million more in tax revenue for fiscal year 1997.
Deputy Mayor Randy Mastro said the extra income, which resulted from growth on Wall Street, would allow the city to remove financial risks from the current budget.
"This is a plan that the rating agencies and the fiscal monitors should love," Mastro said.
The budget modification will include $200 million in 'new needs' and $180 million in agency cuts, he said.
Fiscal monitors have criticized the city for including too many risks in the $33 billion spending plan for the fiscal year that started July 1.

Joseph Lhota, director of the city Office of Management and Budget, said the city would no longer assume it could get $300 million this year from the Port Authority in back rent on the city's airports. The city and Port Authority are in arbitration over the rent claim, which will be postponed to future years under the revised budget.

City officials said the extra income would also allow Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, who runs for re-election next year, to spend more on textbooks for public schools and law enforcement overtime to cover the cost of anti-drug sweeps in Brooklyn and Manhattan.

About half of the $200 million in 'new needs' is for law enforcement overtime, which Mastro attributed to massive anti-narcotics sweeps. And $70 million would fund the mayor's previously announced plan to buy more textbooks for the Board of Education.
